cadence.description: At most one META proposal per 7 days AND per 100 decisions, whichever is longer. After each accepted change, 14 days of observation before the next proposal. This prevents thrashing — the system must live with a change long enough to measure its real effect before changing again.
cadence.emergency_override: The human director may trigger an out-of-cycle META review at any time, or freeze all META proposals indefinitely.

change_protocol.description: How a META observation becomes a live parameter change. Every stage is a gate — failure at any stage stops the proposal.
change_protocol.rollback_threshold: false-ACT rate increase > 0.03 on 30+ new decisions, OR mean realized value drop > 10% vs. pre-change baseline. Either triggers automatic revert.

stages.name: OBSERVE
stages.rule: META runs on schedule (see cadence). It may only propose after the cooldown has elapsed AND minimum sample sizes are met for the target being changed.

stages.name: PROPOSE
stages.rule: Generate the proposal with full evidence: parameter deltas, before/after metrics on training AND held-out sets, sample sizes, confidence, motivating decisions, and the falsifier.

stages.name: DREAM_BACKTEST
stages.rule: Run the proposed parameters through Dream against historical decisions. The proposal must improve held-out prediction accuracy AND not increase the false-ACT rate. If it fails either, the proposal dies here.

stages.name: ADVERSARY_REVIEW
stages.rule: The Permanent Adversary attacks the proposal itself: 'How could this weight change be wrong? Could it be gamed? Does it create a blind spot?' If the adversary finds a substantive flaw, the proposal returns to PROPOSE with the finding attached, or dies.

stages.name: TEAM_REVIEW
stages.rule: Posted to the team board. Seats review the evidence. This is where human judgment meets machine inference.

stages.name: SCORECARD_MERGE
stages.rule: The Scorecard Law governs the merge: enumerate, score, gate, decide, receipt. The human director holds veto at this stage — any META change can be blocked, no justification required beyond the director's judgment.

stages.name: OBSERVE_AND_ROLLBACK
stages.rule: After merge, a mandatory observation window (see cadence). META monitors realized outcomes under the new parameters. If the false-ACT rate rises or realized value drops beyond the rollback threshold, the change is AUTOMATICALLY REVERTED to the previous parameters — no human action required, no debate. The revert itself is logged as a META learning event.

core_question: Not 'what should I do?' but 'how should I decide what to do better?'

epistemic_state.falsifier: If META proposals consistently fail Dream backtesting (the data doesn't support improvement), or if accepted changes consistently trigger rollback (the gates aren't catching bad proposals), the learning method or the safety bounds need redesign.
epistemic_state.note: This is V1 of the META design. The safety architecture is deliberately conservative — bounded deltas, mandatory backtesting, adversary audit, human veto, automatic rollback. The conservatism is the point: a recursive improvement layer that can break the system is worse than no recursive improvement at all. As evidence accumulates that the gates work, bounds can be widened through the same governance process.
open_refinements: Cross-seat calibration: do different seats' decisions need different weights, or is one vector right for all?
Temporal decay: should older decisions count less in the training set? What half-life?
Dimension interaction terms: META-V1 treats dimensions independently; real decisions may have interactions (e.g., urgency × evidence). V2 scope.
Meta-meta evaluation: after N cycles, audit whether META itself is improving decision quality over time — the ultimate validation.

attack_surfaces_for_meta: overfitting — does the proposal memorize noise in the training decisions?
gaming — could a seat exploit the new weights to push through a low-value action?
blind_spot — does the new weight vector systematically undervalue any dimension?
interaction — do the new weights combine badly with any registered heuristic?
drift — does the proposal move the system away from verified human value toward a proxy?
adversary_as_auditor.output_to_meta: Audit report: PASS, PASS_WITH_CONDITIONS (specific modifications required), or FAIL (proposal dies or returns to PROPOSE).
adversary_as_auditor.role: The Adversary audits META's proposals before they go live. It treats every proposal as a suspect: looking for overfitting, gaming vectors, blind spots the new weights would create, and interactions with existing heuristics that could compound badly.

dream_as_experiment_runner.input_from_meta: Proposed parameter set + the historical decision log slice to test against.
dream_as_experiment_runner.output_to_meta: Backtest report: accuracy delta, false-ACT delta, list of flipped decisions with correctness assessment.
dream_as_experiment_runner.role: Dream is META's laboratory. Before any parameter change goes live, Dream backtests it: 'If we had used these weights on the last 200 decisions, what would have changed?' Dream runs counterfactual scoring — same decisions, new math — and reports which decisions would have flipped thresholds and whether those flips would have been correct.

governance_flow.description: META proposals are governance changes and flow through the standard governance pipeline: PR → Scorecard Law → team review → merge → observation. META has no fast lane, no exemptions, no self-approval. The human director's veto is absolute.
governance_flow.versioning: Every accepted META change is versioned (META-CYCLE-NNN). The full parameter history is preserved — the system can always answer 'what were the weights on date X and why did they change?'

input.adversary_findings: Which surfaces fired, what they found, whether the decision changed
input.decision_log: Every scored decision: the 10 dimension scores, S_final, threshold action taken, timestamp, seat, context hash
input.description: META reads the complete decision trail — what was predicted, what was done, what actually happened.
input.dream_backtests: Simulation predictions vs. actual outcomes, per strategy
input.realized_value: Observed verified human value after action, recorded independently (not by the acting seat where possible)

method.held_out_rule: All calibration uses a held-out decision set META has not trained on. Backtesting on training data alone is insufficient — it proves nothing about generalization.
method.step_1_correlate: Compute per-dimension predictive correlation against realized value.
method.step_2_calibrate: Constrained optimization for weight vector minimizing held-out prediction error.
method.step_3_threshold_sweep: ROC analysis for optimal threshold placement.
method.step_7_propose: Generate parameter deltas ONLY where the evidence is strong (see confidence requirements in change_protocol).

output.format: A META proposal: proposed parameter changes, before/after metrics, sample sizes, confidence levels, the specific decisions that motivated each change, and the Dream backtest results.
output.requirement: Every proposal must name the falsifier: what observed evidence would prove this change wrong?

mission: Improve the decision process itself — not what Naya decides, but how well Naya decides.

adversary_surfaces.method: For each adversary surface, compute precision = (attacks that changed a decision or caught a real defect) / (total attacks). Surfaces with precision < 0.05 over 50+ attacks are noise — deprioritize. Surfaces with high precision get more attack budget. Propose reallocation of adversary compute.
adversary_surfaces.question: Which attack surfaces predict bad outcomes? Which are noise?

decision_heuristics.method: The heuristic registry holds rules like 'if reversibility = 1.0, skip extra verification.' For each heuristic, track: invocation count, outcomes when used vs. when not used (matched pairs where possible), and any adversary flags. Heuristics with neutral-or-positive outcomes and zero adversary flags are SAFE. Heuristics correlated with bad outcomes are DANGEROUS — propose removal or tightening.
decision_heuristics.question: Which shortcuts are safe? Which are dangerous?

dream_strategies.method: For each dream simulation strategy, compare its backtest predictions against actual realized outcomes. Accuracy = (predictions within tolerance) / (total predictions). Strategies below 0.60 accuracy get flagged for improvement or retirement. Strategies above 0.80 get promoted to default.
dream_strategies.question: Which simulation methods actually predict real outcomes?

nba_thresholds.method: ROC-style analysis on the decision log: for candidate threshold placements, measure false-ACT rate (acted but realized low value) vs. false-HOLD rate (held but the action would have been valuable). Propose thresholds that minimize the weighted sum of both errors, with false-ACT weighted 2x false-HOLD (acting badly is worse than waiting).
nba_thresholds.question: Are 0.70/0.55/0.40 well-placed?

nba_weights.method: For each dimension, compute the correlation between its score and realized verified human value across the decision log. Dimensions that predict value well earn weight; dimensions that don't predict lose it. Constrained optimization: find the weight vector (summing to 1.0, each within [0.02, 0.35]) that minimizes prediction error on the held-out decision set.
nba_weights.question: Are 0.22/0.18/0.14 right? What does the decision data say?

rationale: The key tension — powerful enough to genuinely improve, constrained enough to never break — is resolved by separating WHAT can change from WHAT cannot, and by making every change prove itself three times before it goes live (Dream backtest, Adversary audit, Scorecard merge) plus once after (observation with automatic rollback). META is powerful inside its sandbox: it can rewrite the scoring math that every seat uses to decide. It is powerless at the foundation: it cannot touch the mission, the gates, the risk threshold, or the law that governs it. The bounded deltas and cooldowns prevent thrashing; the held-out validation prevents overfitting; the anti-gaming rules prevent META from grading its own homework; the recursion limit prevents infinite regress. The human director's absolute veto is the final backstop — not because META is untrusted, but because the mission belongs to the human, and no optimization process may ever outrank that.

anti_gaming.rule_1: META is evaluated on realized human value from independent observation, never on its own scoring. It cannot make itself look good by changing the ruler.
anti_gaming.rule_2: Proposals must validate on held-out decisions, not just the training set. Overfitting to past decisions is the primary failure mode.
anti_gaming.rule_3: META cannot propose changes that reduce adversary coverage or dream backtesting rigor — the oversight mechanisms are load-bearing and META cannot saw them off.
anti_gaming.rule_4: Any proposal that would increase the false-ACT rate on the held-out set is rejected automatically, regardless of other improvements.

change_bounds.description: No single proposal may change any NBA weight by more than 0.05. Large shifts require multiple validated cycles — this prevents a single bad inference from destabilizing decisions.
change_bounds.description_bounds: No dimension may be zeroed out (every dimension earned its place) or allowed to dominate (no single point of failure in judgment).

immutable: human_gates — production dispatch, production DB, credentials/money, destructive/irreversible, constitutional ratification. META can never move, weaken, or bypass these.
risk_gate_threshold — the 0.85 hard gate is sacred. META cannot raise it (which would permit more risk) or lower it (which would paralyze action). It is fixed.
core_mission — 'Maximum Verified Human Value per Moment.' META optimizes HOW decisions serve this; it cannot redefine WHAT the mission is.
scorecard_law — the five-step merge protocol governs META's own changes. META cannot exempt itself.
optimization_function — realized verified human value is the fixed target. META cannot substitute a proxy (e.g., 'decisions per hour' or 'average score') that drifts from human value.
safety.principle: META changes the rules of the game. Every proposal is treated as a governance code change — the most powerful lever in the system, and therefore the most gated.

recursion_limit.rule: META-V1 adjusts PARAMETERS (weights, thresholds, surface priorities). It does NOT adjust its own LEARNING METHOD — the correlation/optimization procedure is fixed. Changing how META learns is a constitutional-level change requiring human director approval.
recursion_limit.why: Unbounded recursion (META improving META improving META) is unstable. One fixed layer of learning-method, with parameters free to move inside safety bounds, gives genuine improvement without infinite regress.
